text: This report addresses an appeal concerning one variance sought respecting a proposal for two illuminated window signs displaying static copy (the "Proposed Signs"). The Proposed Signs are to be located on the first storey of the north and east elevations of the multi-storey, mixed-use building at the property municipally known as 1093 Queen Street West (the "Premises"). The purpose of the signs is to identify the "Rexall" drugstore on the ground floor. The variance application was originally applied for by Christina Wiggins of Jones Neon Displays Ltd. (the "Applicant"). After conducting a review in accordance with the requirements of the Sign By-law, a decision was made to refuse to grant the requested variance. Subsequently, the Applicant filed an appeal of the decision. It has been determined that there was not enough information provided to establish that the Proposed Signs meet all…

The Sign Variance Committee: 1. Refused to grant the requested variance for the Proposed Signs at the premises municipally known as 1093 Queen Street West, as described in Attachment 1 of the report (August 29, 2018) from the Manager, Sign By-law Unit, Toronto Building.
